final.answer: For pump P-1-2, the pump specifications list a maximum operating temperature limit of 37 °C (100 °F), with a note to consult the factory for applications exceeding the indicated maximum pressure and/or temperature. The seal detail separately allows a maximum temperature of liquid pumped of 71 °C (160 °F). So the hottest liquid you can put through it is 37 °C (100 °F) per the pump's operating limit (the seal can tolerate up to 71 °C / 160 °F).

final.answer: Yes — GV-10-1 is a solenoid valve (type 165, 2/2-way, PVC-U) and its coil needs electrical power. The valve is available with supply voltages of 24V DC, 230V AC (50/60 Hz) and 110V AC, with a voltage tolerance of ±10%. So either 24 V DC or 230 V AC will work, but only if the matching coil is fitted: which one is correct is decided by the coil actually installed on the valve, and the manufacturer's instruction is to use the voltage and current type given on the type plate (AC coils also carry a risk-of-injury warning). If you need to change voltage, separate coil sets (spare parts) are offered for each of the three voltages.

final.answer: FV-106-2 is a Fisher easy-e globe control valve, and per its datasheet the flow characteristic depends on the cage chosen. With standard cages you can get quick-opening, linear, or equal percentage. With Whisper Trim, WhisperFlo, or Cavitrol cages the characteristic is linear only. The ET trim cartridge option offers equal percentage or linear. So all three characteristics you ask about — equal percentage, linear, and quick opening — are available, with the choice made through the trim/cage selection at ordering or configuration.

The standard 'ET' variant is not listed in Table 17 for the 2 inch size in these facts, and no Cv values specifically labelled 'at full open' were found beyond these maximum-travel values.

args.question: What is the Cv at full open for a 2 inch valve?

final.answer: For valve FV-10-2, the datasheet lists the available body, bonnet and bonnet spacer/bottom-flange materials as: cast iron, WCC carbon steel, LCC carbon steel, WC9 chrome-moly steel, CF8M (cast 316 stainless steel), CF3M (cast 316L stainless steel), and other materials upon request. Yes, stainless steel is offered — in two grades, CF8M (316) and CF3M (316L) — which would be suitable choices for corrosive service. Note that stainless bodies are available with RF/RTJ flanged CL150/300/600, screwed, butt-weld and socket-weld connections, while cast iron is limited to CL125/CL250 flanged; and in all cases the pressure/temperature rating of the body material must not be exceeded regardless of trim capabilities.

final.answer: FT-104-2 is tested per IEC 60770-1:1999 for field or pipeline installation with a high vibration level. The test conditions are a frequency range of 10-60 Hz with a 0.21 mm peak displacement amplitude, and 60-2000 Hz at 3g. final.answer: FIC-104-2 operates control valve FV-104-2, which is described by a Fisher easy-e valve bulletin (ET/EAT/ETR family). The available trim options for this family are: standard metal trims 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 27, 28, 29, 37/37H, 57 and 316L (with variants 37H for temperatures above 210°C and 4C/29C/57C for PTFE seating); NACE sour-service trims 85, 85C, 86, 87, 87C; Trim Cartridge trims (1TC, 27TC, 29TC, 85TC, 87TC); DST (dirty service) trim; Cavitrol III trim (trim 76, one- and two-stage cages); and Whisper noise-attenuation trims (Whisper Trim I, Whisper Trim III, Whisper NXG Trim and WhisperFlo cages). The trims for high pressure drop or noise are the Whisper trims/cages, which provide aerodynamic noise attenuation for gaseous service, and the Cavitrol III trim (trim 76), which protects against cavitation at high pressure drops in liquid service.

Its weights are given on the specification sheet: net weight 194 lbs (88 kg) and shipping weight 204 lbs (93 kg), with an export crate size of 5.6 cu ft (0.16 cu m). An outline dimension drawing exists (front and side view, in inches/millimeters) showing the discharge flange (19 mm holes on a 139.7 mm bolt circle), suction flange (8 holes on a 190.5 mm bolt circle), keyway and base holes/slots, but the description does not provide the pump's overall length, width and height values. Therefore whether it fits on a 1 m by 0.6 m base cannot be determined from the available information.

final.answer: The item directly upstream of BV-103-1 is GV-103-1. For this item, the seal/gasket material is given as EPDM (the specifications list 'Gasket material = EPDM, FKM'). However, the description contains no information about the material of its body, so the body material cannot be determined. Since EPDM gaskets are specified, the seal material conflicts with your fluid's attack on EPDM — EPDM would not be suitable.

final.answer: The item directly downstream of BV-103-1 is pump P-103-2. Its pump specifications list bearing lubrication as SAE 30 non-detergent oil with a standard bearing housing level oiler, and the seal detail notes a mechanical, self-lubricated seal. The description does not state any grease type or a greasing frequency, so how often the bearings need greasing cannot be determined from the provided information.

final.answer: GV-1-2 is a globe valve in the discharge line from pump P-1-1, upstream of ball valve PV-1-1. A globe valve passing fluid when it should be shut is usually caused by seat or disc damage — wear, erosion, or debris (e.g., a particle or weld slug) lodged on the sealing face — or a stem/disc connection failure that prevents the disc from seating. Fix it by closing upstream and downstream isolation (note PV-1-1 downstream) and depressurizing/draining the line, then inspect: lap or re-seat the disc and seat ring or replace the trim, replace the gasket if the leak is at the bonnet or flanges, and verify the disc is properly attached to the stem and the valve is fully turned to the closed position before returning to service.
